topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Visualizing Conic Sections
target_audience: High school students or undergraduate geometry students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Plane-Cone Intersection
lecture_lines: Imagine a double-napped cone sliced by a plane.
The cutting angle determines the shape of the slice.
We get circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
animations: Display a double-napped cone (#FFFFFF) and an intersecting plane (#FF9900).
Rotate the plane to show a circle (#00FF00) and then an ellipse (#00FF00).
Rotate the plane to show a parabola (#00FF00) and then a hyperbola (#00FF00).

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: We place spheres inside the cone.
These spheres touch both the cone and plane.
Tangency points are the keys to conic geometry.
animations: Display a cone (#FFFFFF) and an inscribed sphere (#3399FF).
Bring a cutting plane (#FF9900) to touch the sphere.
Highlight the point of tangency between sphere and plane using a small, high-contrast marker (#FF0000, scale_factor 0.3).

sections.title: Geometric Proof: The Ellipse Case
lecture_lines: Pick a point on our ellipse.
Distance to foci equals segment length.
Sums of these lengths stay constant.
This proves the classic ellipse definition.
The geometry is beautiful and simple.
animations: Show an elliptical cross-section with two Dandelin spheres (#3399FF).
Trace the distance from a point on the ellipse to the spheres' tangency points (#FFFFFF).
Demonstrate constant sum of these distances (#FF9900).
Emphasize the constant property with a flashing animation of the sum result (#FF9900).
Complete the proof showing the segment length invariance (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Generalizing to Parabola and Hyperbola
lecture_lines: Parabolas need just one single sphere.
Hyperbolas require spheres in both nappes.
The plane cuts through the entire cone.
animations: Show a single sphere for a parabolic intersection (#3399FF).
Show two spheres, one in each cone nappe, for a hyperbola (#3399FF).
Highlight the distinct tangency points for these geometries (#FF0000, scale_factor 0.3).

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Conic sections appear in nature everywhere.
From orbital paths to architectural acoustics.
Dandelin spheres reveal their hidden logic.
animations: Display a Whispering Gallery room layout (#FFFFFF).
Animate sound waves bouncing between two elliptical focal points (#FF9900).
Fade out to show orbital mechanics planetary paths (#3399FF).
